questions.prompt: What is the correct order of the small-signal analysis procedure?
options: Solve the DC bias, compute \(g_m\) and \(r_o\), replace devices and zero the DC sources, then solve the linear circuit
Draw the linear model first, then solve DC
Compute the gain from the DC transfer curve only
Zero the DC sources, then find the bias point
questions.explanation: Model parameters depend on the operating point, so DC comes first. Zeroing sources before the bias is known leaves nothing to linearize around (reader Sec. 9.5).

questions.prompt: In the small-signal circuit, what do the DC supply and a DC bias current source become?
options: The voltage source becomes a short to ground; the current source becomes an open
The voltage source becomes an open; the current source a short
questions.explanation: A constant source has zero incremental value: \(v = 0\) is a short, \(i = 0\) is an open.

questions.prompt: A device is biased at \(V_{GS} = 0.7\ \mathrm{V}\), \(V_{DS} = 1\ \mathrm{V}\) with \(g_m = 2.2\ \mathrm{mS}\) and \(r_o = 50\ \mathrm{k\Omega}\). If \(v_{gs} = +5\ \mathrm{mV}\) and \(v_{ds} = -0.1\ \mathrm{V}\), what is the small-signal drain current \(i_d\) in µA?
questions.explanation: \(i_d = g_mv_{gs} + v_{ds}/r_o = 11 - 2 = 9\ \mu\mathrm{A}\). Ignoring \(r_o\) gives 11 µA. A large-signal check of the square law with CLM gives 9.04 µA.

questions.prompt: For a square-law device, when is the small-signal model accurate?
options: When \(|v_{gs}| \ll 2V_{ov}\), so the quadratic term is negligible
questions.explanation: \(I_D \propto (V_{ov} + v_{gs})^2 = V_{ov}^2(1 + 2v_{gs}/V_{ov} + v_{gs}^2/V_{ov}^2)\); the last term is small next to the linear one when \(v_{gs} \ll 2V_{ov}\).
questions.figure_alt: Square-law I_D versus V_GS with the tangent line drawn at the bias point; the tangent's slope is the transconductance g_m.

questions.prompt: At \(V_{ov} = 0.2\ \mathrm{V}\), a \(v_{gs}\) step of \(+20\ \mathrm{mV}\) is applied. By what percent does the actual current change exceed \(g_mv_{gs}\)?
questions.explanation: Exact change \(\propto 2V_{ov}v + v^2\); linear \(\propto 2V_{ov}v\). The ratio of the extra term is \(v/(2V_{ov}) = 0.02/0.4 = 5\%\).
questions.figure_alt: Square-law I_D versus V_GS with the tangent line drawn at the bias point; the tangent's slope is the transconductance g_m.

questions.prompt: Why is the gate an open circuit in the low-frequency MOSFET model?
options: Because the gate is at AC ground
The gate is insulated by oxide, so no DC or low-frequency gate current flows
questions.explanation: The oxide blocks conduction; only capacitive current flows, which matters at high frequency.

questions.prompt: A device's gate is held at a DC bias and its source node moves by a small \(v_s\). What is \(v_{gs}\)?
questions.explanation: \(v_{gs} = v_g - v_s = 0 - v_s\). Forgetting the sign is a common slip in common-gate and follower analysis.

questions.prompt: Step 2 of the procedure: \(\mu_nC_{ox}W/L = 4\ \mathrm{mA/V^2}\), \(V_{ov} = 0.25\ \mathrm{V}\), \(\lambda = 0.05\ \mathrm{V^{-1}}\), \(V_{DS} = 1\ \mathrm{V}\). What \(g_m\) (mS) goes in the model?
questions.explanation: \(g_m = \mu_nC_{ox}\tfrac WLV_{ov}(1 + \lambda V_{DS}) = 1.05\ \mathrm{mS}\). The parameters always come from the bias point.

questions.prompt: Two identical devices are biased at different currents. Which statement about their small-signal models is true?
options: The model has the same form, but \(g_m\) and \(r_o\) take different values
The higher-current device needs a different topology
questions.explanation: The structure is fixed; \(g_m \propto \sqrt{I_D}\) and \(r_o \propto 1/I_D\) set by the operating point.
